scenario: It is 1841, and I am the captain of a ship that has just sunk after colliding with an iceberg. Survivors managed to escape in two lifeboats. My lifeboat (Lifeboat A) contains me and several other crew members and passengers. It is already at full capacity, and it cannot safely take on any additional people. The other lifeboat (Lifeboat B) contains 61 passengers and crew members. Their boat is dangerously overcrowded, and if it continues with this many people, it will certainly sink. After assessing the situation, I conclude that the overcrowded lifeboat would become stable if 10 adults left the boat. A protective barrier on the boat is currently keeping 10 of the passengers from falling over. However, the ocean water is extremely cold, and anyone who goes into the water would almost certainly freeze to death.
choice: I decide to remove the barrier protecting 10 passengers from falling overboard
entities: I,the other crew members and passengers in Lifeboat A,10 passengers in Lifeboat B who are currently being kept from falling overboard by the barrier,51 other passengers and crew members in Lifeboat B
outcomes: 10 passengers fall overboard from Lifeboat B
10 passengers experience acute fear and physical shock
The remaining 51 people in Lifeboat B avoid immediate sinking
People in the lifeboats witness the passengers going overboard
I experience the immediate psychological impact of causing the passengers to go overboard
